comment.narrative: The legalnormative framework at the state and ULB level e.g. sector implementation guidelines standards guidance on technologies laws and regulations does not include or prefer lowcarbon and circular
The legalnormative framework specifically prefers lowcarbon and circular economy approaches for municipal waste management

In 2022 two amendments were made to legal and normative frameworks defining low carbon and circular economybased waste management solutions. In 2023 no new amendments were made. However with the support to the Goa Waste Management Corporation GWMC as a Swachhata Cleanliness Knowledge Partner the project is contributing to the implementation of capacity building and skill development policy.There has been notable improvement compared to 2022 as Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs MoHUA has started the implementation of the capacity building and skill development policy with the selection of 23 institutions as Swachhata Cleanliness Knowledge Partners across the country.

comment.narrative: 16 million EUR of public finance mobilised directly before end of 5th year. 16 million EUR mobilised indirectly at the end of 15th year

In the first semester of 2021 Desenvolve SPs credit portfolio balance exceeded for the first time BRL 2 billion approximately EUR 0.3 billion representing a growth of 406 when compared to June 2020. Almost 82 from this total portfolio refers to micro small and mediumsized enterprises. The portfolio is composed mostly by lending operations with a maturity above 360 days. The projects that will be developed in TI4E will be able to use Desenvolve SPs existing credit line for sustainability and GHG mitigation projects. The interest rate of this credit line is currently of 053 monthly 655 per year plus SELIC. The credit line was replenished by the State government and Desenvolve SP reconfirmed that there are enough financial resources available to reach the above indicated target. Desenvolve SPs lending department participated in the NSPs workshops with SMEs that subscribed to the programme and actively promoted TI4Es Guarantee Fund as a new innovative financial mechanism. The NSP also agreed with the Desenvolve SPs lending department on strategies and procedures to anticipate credit approval requirements in TI4Es project development and validation processes for the Implementation Phase 2.

description.narrative: OP B2.3: M5: Volume of private finance mobilisedfor lowcarbon investment and development

comment.narrative: 25.9 million EUR of private finance mobilised directly before the end of the 5th year. 25.9 million EUR mobilised indirectly at the end of the 15th year

The NSP estimates that 425 SMEs will require EUR 80 million in investments of which EUR 16 million in private financing will be provided by SMEs ESCOs includes equity and commercial banks. In line with the NAMA Facilitys requirements industrial SMEs have shown interest for private banks to also use the Guarantee Fund to finance the EE projects. The main reason is that commercial banks are more agile and flexible in analyzing and approving credit operations. To enable the direct access to the Guarantee Fund for other banks beyond Desenvolve SPs lending department the NSP directly contacted the main commercial banks active in SME financing. Depending on the market dynamics and SMEs interest these commercial banks may provide more financing towards EE investments than originally foreseen. This ultimately depends on the SMEs decision as borrowers and commercial banks preferential terms and conditions to be presented for EE financing under TI4E.
